definition: Elated means overjoyed — filled with a joy that lifts you, usually right after big good news.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word elated. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know elated should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Elated by the acceptance letter, Tomas read it aloud twice and taped it to the refrigerator at eye level.
Pleased is quiet satisfaction — a nod and a small smile, several floors below elated.
Delighted is real, sparkling happiness, but elated is stronger — joy with altitude, joy that wants to shout.

Overjoyed is elated's nearest plain twin: flooded with more joy than you know what to do with. If they differ at all, it is the picture — overjoyed is a flood filling you up, elated is lift, joy carrying you upward. In most sentences either word would serve.

Thrilled is joy with a jolt of excitement running through it — a shiver, a racing pulse, the fun of the moment itself. Elated is more lift than voltage: the floating fullness that follows big good news. A roller coaster leaves you thrilled; an acceptance letter leaves you elated.

Jubilant is joy at full volume and usually in company — the roar of a winning locker room, fists in the air over a triumph. Elated can be perfectly private: one person floating on one piece of good news. Jubilation celebrates a victory out loud; elation only needs the news.
